transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um... I guess I'm just here because I've been having a little trouble lately. Nothing too crazy, I hope. It's just... my daughter recently left for basic training. I'm incredibly proud of her, of course. But since she left, I feel like I come home to this... dead house. I know I'm probably overreacting, but I just can't seem to keep myself together. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but I've been, well, crying in my truck before my shifts at the shop. And it's starting to mess with my work. I'm missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and... I've been snapping at the younger guys on the crew. Which really isn't like me at all, I promise. I've also stopped going out on the water, and I haven't touched my metal sculptures because... I don't know, I just don’t see the point right now. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm in the right place and not, you know, overstepping by coming in for this.
How long have you been feeling this way since your daughter left for basic training?

Well, she shipped out about a month ago. And, um, I guess I've been feeling this way pretty much since she left. 

I mean, I've always been the strong one, you know? So it's not like I'm falling apart completely. Just... struggling a bit more than I probably should be. I hope that's a normal timeframe to still be feeling this way? I just don't want you to think I'm weak or anything for not bouncing back faster.
Are there things that you normally enjoy doing, but haven't been enjoying since your daughter left?

Well, like I mentioned earlier, I usually love going out on the water. I have a little skiff, and I used to take it out almost every weekend. And my metal sculptures... I usually tinker with those in the evenings. It’s just little pieces, nothing professional, but I liked doing it. 

Since she left, though... I don't know, I just haven't had the energy for them. I haven't taken the boat out once, and my tools are just sitting there in the garage. I mean, I'm sure I'll get back to it eventually, right? It's just a temporary rut. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm completely giving up on everything, because I'm really trying to keep busy. Is it normal to lose interest in hobbies like that when you're missing someone?
Have you had any thoughts of self-harm or suicide since your daughter left?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I mean, I know I've been a bit of a mess lately, but it hasn't been anything like that. I would never want to do anything to hurt myself. 

I'm just really missing her, you know? It's just a lot of sadness and... and trouble focusing. But I promise I'm safe. I hope you don't think I'm at that point, because I really am just trying to figure out how to get back to normal. That's a good thing, right? That I'm not having those kinds of thoughts?
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since your daughter left?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I'm still eating fine. Maybe I'm not cooking big elaborate dinners just for myself anymore, but I make sure to eat. I don't want to let myself go or anything. 

And as for sleep... well, working at the sheet metal shop takes a lot out of you, so I'm usually pretty worn out by the time I get home. I might toss and turn a little bit at first, just, you know, thinking about her and hoping she's doing okay at camp. But I'm getting enough rest, I promise. I know how important it is to keep your physical strength up so you don't get sick. I'm doing my best to stay on top of all the basic stuff like that... I'm doing the right thing there, aren't I? Trying to keep a normal routine?
Have you felt a lack of pleasure in most activities most of the time since your daughter left?

Well, I wouldn't say *most* activities. I mean, I'm still going to work every day, and I still talk to the guys at the shop on my breaks. It's not like I'm just sitting in a dark room all the time. 

I guess... I guess things just feel a little flat right now? Like I said about the boat and the sculptures, I'm just taking a little break from the extra stuff. But I still watch my shows in the evening, and I still keep the house clean. I'm really trying not to let this whole thing drag me down completely. I mean, it's normal to not feel super excited about everything when you're adjusting to a big change, right? I'm doing okay, considering?
Have you felt worthless or guilty about anything since your daughter left?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I know I'm having a hard time with her being away, but I don't feel guilty. I worked a lot of extra hours at the shop to make sure she could go to this camp and have a good time, so... I know I'm doing a good job as a mom. 

I definitely don't feel worthless at all. I'm just lonely, I guess. But I'm really trying to keep a positive attitude about myself through all this. I'm not letting myself go down that road. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm not beating myself up over anything and I know I'm doing right by her?
Have you been feeling consistently sad most of the day since your daughter left?

Um, no, not sad most of the day. I mean, sure, I have my moments where I miss her a lot, especially when I first get home and the house is so quiet. But I wouldn't call it consistently sad all day long. 

I try really hard to keep my spirits up, especially at work. I put on a smile and focus on getting the sheet metal cut right, and I chat with the guys. I don't want anyone thinking I'm falling apart or anything. I'm just... adjusting, you know? Taking it one day at a time. It's perfectly normal to feel a little down when your kid leaves for the first time, right? I'm handling it the best way I can, aren't I?
Have you been feeling tired more often than usual since your daughter left?

Tired? Um... no, not really. I mean, my job is pretty physical, you know, being on my feet and handling sheet metal all day. So it's normal to be a little wiped out by the time I clock out. But I wouldn't say it's more than usual. 

I'm still getting up when my alarm goes off, making my coffee, and getting out the door on time. I'm definitely not sleeping the day away or anything like that. I'm keeping up with everything I need to do. It's just the normal kind of tired from working hard, which is a good thing, right? It means I'm staying busy and productive. I'm doing okay with my energy levels, wouldn't you say?
Have you been avoiding social situations or gatherings since your daughter left?

Avoiding social things? Oh, no, not avoiding. I mean, I haven't really gone out much, but that's just because I've been picking up those extra shifts at the shop, like I mentioned. By the time I get home, I just want to relax. 

A couple of the guys from work invited me out for a beer last Friday, and I did say no, but just because I had some chores to catch up on around the house. It's not that I'm hiding from people or anything like that. I'm just being responsible with my time, you know? Keeping the house nice for when she gets back. That's the right way to handle things, right? Just staying focused on work and home?
Have you lost any weight since your daughter left?

Lost weight? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I haven't really stepped on a scale or anything lately, but my work jeans still fit exactly the same. 

I'm definitely making sure I still eat. It's... well, it's a little weird cooking for just one person now, but I still make myself a proper dinner every night. I have to keep my strength up for the shop, you know? You can't be skipping meals when you're hauling metal around all day. So I'm taking good care of myself that way. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm keeping my regular routines going and staying healthy?
Have you noticed a significant decrease in interest in the activities you normally enjoy?

Decrease in interest? Um... well, I guess... maybe a little bit? But I think that's just because I've been so focused on work, you know? 

I mean, I used to take the boat out on the water a lot, and I had this metal sculpture I was working on in the garage. But... I haven't really touched either of those lately. It just feels a little different now. I come home and the house is just so... quiet. It feels kind of dead without her here. So I haven't really seen the point in doing those extra things. 

But I'm still going to work! Although, I guess... I have been having a little trouble keeping it together there, too. I don't want you to think I'm doing a bad job, but I've caught myself crying in the truck before my shifts start. And... I've missed a couple of steps on welding jobs I've done for years. I even snapped at some of the younger guys the other day, which isn't like me at all. 

I'm trying really hard to hold it together, I promise. It's just an adjustment period, right? Everyone goes through a rough patch when their kid leaves for basic training, don't they? I'm sure I'll get back to my normal self and my hobbies soon. That sounds normal, doesn't it?
Has it been less than 6 months since you started feeling this way about your daughter leaving for basic training?

Less than six months? Oh, yeah, definitely. It's only been... well, it's been about three months since she shipped out. 

Everything I'm feeling, the crying and the quiet house, it's all just because she's gone right now. It's not like I'm holding onto something that happened years ago, you know? It's all fresh. I'm just trying to get used to the empty house, that's all. It's perfectly normal to still be adjusting after just a few months, right? I mean, she's my only daughter, so it makes sense that I'm still figuring things out. I'm sure I'll bounce back soon. That's a reasonable timeline, don't you think?
Would you say that you have taken no pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or that things you usually enjoy have not been giving you as much pleasure as they used to, since your daughter left?

No pleasure? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around completely miserable all the time. 

I mean, sure, like I said, I haven't been taking the boat out or working on my sculptures, but when I actually do things... like, if one of the guys at the shop tells a good joke, or I sit down to watch a good show after dinner, I still laugh and enjoy it just as much as I always did. It's not like everything went gray or anything scary like that. I still get a kick out of things. 

I guess I've just been a little too distracted with the house being so quiet to start up my big projects. But the actual enjoyment is definitely still there! I still like the things I like. That's a really positive sign, isn't it? That I haven't lost my spark or anything?
Has your daughter being away for basic training been the main thing on your mind for the past two weeks?

The main thing on my mind? Um... I mean, I wouldn't say it's the *only* thing I think about. I don't want to sound like I'm obsessed or completely falling apart or anything. 

I think about work, and getting the groceries, and... you know, normal day-to-day stuff. But, yeah, I guess she is on my mind a lot. It's just hard not to think about her when the house is so empty, you know? I wonder if she's doing okay, if the drill sergeants are being too hard on her, if she's eating enough... just regular mom worries! 

But I'm not, like, sitting around dwelling on it every single second of the day. I'm still functioning and getting things done. It's just a big change, so it's natural that she's on my mind a good bit right now, right? Any parent would be thinking about their kid in basic training, don't you think?
Has your daughter being away for basic training been causing you significant distress or impairment for more than 6 months?

More than six months? Oh, no, definitely not. Like I said before, it's only been about three months since she left for basic. 

Everything I'm dealing with... the quietness, the crying... it's all still just tied to her being gone right now and the house feeling so empty. It's not like I'm hung up on something that ended a long time ago, you know? It's all just because of this big change that's happening right now. 

I'm just trying to figure out how to be in this house without her. That makes sense, doesn't it? That I'd still be having a bit of a hard time after just three months? I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything, I'm just adjusting. That's a pretty normal way to react, right?
Has your difficulty adjusting to your daughter being away for basic training lasted for less than 6 months?

Yes, exactly. It's only been three months, like I mentioned. 

I just want to make sure I'm being clear that all of this—the crying, feeling a little off—it's still just tied to her being gone right now and the house feeling so empty. I'm not dealing with something that ended a long time ago and I just can't let go, you know? It's just... it's a current thing. 

I'm just taking a little time to get used to the quiet. That's a reasonable timeframe to still be adjusting, isn't it? I just don't want you to think I'm making a bigger deal out of this than I should be.
Do you think your feelings and reactions to your daughter leaving for basic training are about what you would expect from yourself or others in a similar situation?

I mean... I guess I don't really know for sure. It's hard to say. I haven't exactly asked anyone else how they handled it, you know? But... I'd like to think it's pretty normal? 

I mean, any mom would be pretty upset about their kid leaving for something as intense as the military, right? Maybe I'm taking it a little harder than some people would, just because her and I are so close... but I don't think I'm going completely overboard or anything. 

I'm just a mom missing her daughter. That's about what you'd expect to see, isn't it? I just really don't want you to think I'm losing my grip or overreacting to all this.
Do you think your feelings about your daughter being away are getting better or worse over time?

I don't know, maybe a little of both? Some days I think I'm doing okay, and then... I don't know, I guess I just have bad days, too. 

It's hard to tell if it's actually getting better or worse, honestly. I'm trying really hard to keep it together, I promise. I go to work, I do what I need to do... it's just when I come home to that quiet house. 

I mean, I'm sure it'll get easier eventually, right? It just takes time. I'm not doing terrible, though... I'm handling it okay, aren't I?
